A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEM study and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–11, Figures 1–7, and Appendices A–F. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments on FLUX and SD3, including safety, retention, runtime, ablation results, and qualitative generations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons and the appendix sensitivity analyses and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: GEM retains the same teacher/student setup, target-trajectory sampling, early-timestep supervision, and contrastive velocity objective in Equations 13–14. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same safety and rights-protection scenarios, benchmark prompt sets, MS COCO utility evaluation, identities, fictional characters, and qualitative style-erasure examples. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: ESD, UCE, Concept Ablation, EraseAnything, and EraseFlow retain the same experiment-specific participation. For example, Table 2 includes all five, while the SD3 comparison in Table 6 still includes only ESD and EraseFlow.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendices B–E retain the same model configurations, training budgets, sampling procedures, classifier thresholds, sample counts, and evaluation metrics. The editorial changes do not revise experimental settings.

E4.justification: The loss-reduction ablation in Table 1, offset experiment in Figure 6, hyperparameter and target-prompt analyses in Tables 7–10, and supplementary qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same run-to-run variability reporting, and Appendix E.3 retains the same generation-seed description. No uncertainty estimates, statistical procedures, or run-count disclosures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative samples match, including appendix results. For example, GEM's T2I-RP unsafe rates remain 19.63% for nudity in Table 2 and 50.77% for gore in Table 3.

T1.justification: The trajectory-balance reduction, velocity-matching derivation, equations, and Appendix A qualifications about densities and surrogate transitions remain mathematically unchanged. Appendix wording corrections do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unifying erasure objectives, approximately fivefold faster erasure, stronger safety performance, and improved retention. Removing duplicated wording does not change claim scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the erasure–utility tradeoff, UCE's strengths on fictional characters, and category interference are unchanged. Section 7 and Appendix A retain the same evaluation limitations and theoretical qualifications.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimizer and LoRA specifications, hyperparameters, baseline adaptations, evaluation prompts, and code-reference information remain unchanged. The corrected correspondence addresses do not revise technical reproduction or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including GEM's relationship to teacher-guided erasure and GFlowNet-based approaches. No references or substantive novelty comparisons are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds missing '.de' suffixes to correspondence addresses, corrects 'Trajectoy' in Appendix A, removes duplicated 'prompts' in the conclusion, and makes several grammar, punctuation, and spelling edits. Section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small local spacing and line-break adjustments, including in the correspondence text and conclusion. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–11 retain their content, captions, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: The corrected correspondence addresses, appendix heading, duplicated wording, and grammar modestly improve editorial accuracy and readability. Scientific arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is small and editorial.
